sections.name: File setup
sections.title: Build and publish jobs
sections.what: Has two jobs. The first builds the site and uploads it. The second publishes it to Pages. Only one publish runs at a time.
sections.why: Likely reason: splitting build and publish follows the usual Pages pattern, and the one-at-a-time rule prevents overlapping deploys.
sections.watch_out: The out folder and the page URL look wrong for this app, so check the first run's log.

summary: Builds the app and publishes it to GitHub Pages when app code changes on the main branch.
purpose: Puts a site online on GitHub Pages automatically.
why: Likely reason: automatic publishing after app code changes saves manual steps.
how: 1. Runs on a push to main that changes app files, package.json or next.config.js, or when started by hand. 2. Installs Node 20 and the packages. 3. Builds the app. 4. Uploads the out folder. 5. Publishes it to Pages.
inputs: The code on the main branch and the build output.
risks: The app uses server routes and login, which a static Pages site cannot run. No static export is set in next.config.js, so the out folder may not be created, and the deploy would likely fail. The page URL reads a step output from another job, which may be empty. Changes only to middleware or lib files do not trigger a deploy.
debug: If the upload fails, check whether the out folder exists after the build step. If the site is blank or login fails, the hosting target may be wrong, so compare with the Vercel setup.
